faqs.a: The ceiling is 42, raised from 35 in April 2026 under Army Regulation 601-210, effective 20 April 2026. The minimum is 17 with parental consent, or 18 otherwise. The change aligns the Army with the Air Force, Space Force and Coast Guard, targeting older applicants with civilian technical skills for warrant officer and specialist roles.

For technical jobs like cyber, intelligence or aviation maintenance, aim for 50 or above, since stronger line scores unlock enlistment bonuses of up to $50,000.

headline: Join the US Army in 2026: Enlistment Requirements and Bonuses
metaDescription: US Army recruitment 2026: age limit raised to 42, ASVAB minimum 31, enlistment bonuses up to $50,000, Green Card eligibility and officer rules explained.

sections.content:
To enlist in the US Army in 2026, you must be between 17 and 42 years old, with parental consent required at 17. The April 2026 change, codified in Army Regulation 601-210, raised the ceiling from 35 for the first time in a decade, opening the door to older candidates with civilian technical experience.

You must also be a US citizen or a lawful permanent resident with a valid Green Card, hold a high school diploma or GED, pass the MEPS medical exam and physical fitness standards, and score at least 31 on the ASVAB's AFQT section. Single prior convictions for marijuana possession or drug paraphernalia no longer require a separate Pentagon waiver.
sections.title: Who Can Enlist: Age, Citizenship and Education

sections.content:
The ASVAB decides both whether you get in and which of the Army's 150-plus MOS career fields you can choose. An AFQT of 31 is the floor, while a score of 50 or above qualifies you for most jobs across the Army. Competitive fields like cyber operations, intelligence analysis and aviation maintenance set higher line-score requirements on top of that.

Higher scores also mean bigger money. Enlistment bonuses scale with ASVAB performance and the Army's needs: entry-level roles carry little or no bonus, standard technical roles around $5,000 to $15,000, and top-tier specialties such as cryptologic linguists or special forces candidates up to $50,000. Serious ASVAB preparation is one of the highest-return investments an applicant can make.
sections.title: The ASVAB, MOS Selection and Bonuses

sections.content:
The standard enlistment pipeline has about ten steps and typically runs three to nine months. It starts with researching branches and contacting a recruiter, then the PiCAT pre-test taken at home, followed by the full ASVAB and medical examination at a Military Entrance Processing Station, or MEPS.

After qualifying, you select your MOS, sign the DD Form 4 enlistment contract and enter the Delayed Entry Program until your ship date. The Army runs the largest recruiting mission of any service, so it handles the broadest range of applicants, but competitive cycles still reward early preparation and high test scores.
